before: Explicit tracks are declared in the template. Grid creates implicit tracks when additional items need space beyond that template.

The HTML supplies the elements; CSS supplies their presentation. This small fixture uses horizontal writing and left-to-right direction. ```html
One
Two
Three
``` ```css .demo { writing-mode: horizontal-tb; direction: ltr; } .grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 100px 100px; grid-template-rows: 40px; grid-auto-rows: 60px; gap: 0; } ```

grid-template-columns declares two columns; grid-template-rows: 40px declares one row. The third item needs another row. grid-auto-rows: 60px sizes that implicit row, leaving the explicit row at 40px. Default row auto-placement follows the HTML order in this fixture.
Use auto-row sizing for a growing set of cards. Avoid dense packing when it would confuse visual and keyboard order; placing an item far outside the template can create additional implicit tracks.
Keep the explicit row 40px tall and make the extra row 60px tall.
after: A grid track is a row or a column. An explicit track is one you list in the template. An implicit track is an extra one Grid creates when it needs more space.
The first two items fit in the first row. The third item needs a new row. `grid-auto-rows: 60px` makes that extra row 60 pixels tall.
If you change `grid-auto-rows` to 90 pixels, only the extra row becomes taller. The first row keeps its own 40-pixel setting.
Auto-row sizing helps when more cards are added later. Keep their visual order easy to follow alongside their HTML order.
Keep the first row 40 pixels tall. Make the extra row 60 pixels tall.
